newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: RUGBY UNION-SLOPPY ENGLAND LOSE 23-21 TO BUENOS AIRES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SLOPPY ENGLAND LOSE 23-21 TO BUENOS AIRES.

text.p: A weakened England lost 23-21 to a Buenos Aires fortified by eight Argentina squad members on Saturday, as Alex King and Mark Mapletoft missed all but two of their ten kicks for penalties and conversions.

England started briskly enough on a cold southern hemisphere autumn's day, hustling into Buenos Aires territory for King to boot in two penalties in the first minutes. But it was all downhill from then on for King, who fluffed all his remaining chances -- three conversions and a penalty.

King looked disturbed by the basically genteel barracking from the 6,500-strong upper crust crowd at the Buenos Aires Cricket and Rugby Club and he was replaced late in the second half by Mapletoft. Mapletoft proved just as good at missing, and notched up four squandered penalties.

But the marksmanship of Buenos Aires number 10 Jose Cilley, who is in the Argentina squad for next Saturday's first test, was less forgiving. He scored five penalties and one quick smart drop goal, missing only the conversion for a try by fellow Puma Tomas Solari.
Ben Clark responded with brutal speed to the Buenos Aires try, scoring his own about a minute later to tie the match at 11-11 at half time.

Captain Phil de Glanville also scored a try to keep England in contention, and then Jim Mallinder capped a solid personal game by tearing down over the left corner of the touchline for another five points.
England was effective in the scrum, and Nigel Redman sailed up to win most of his lineouts. But a fast-paced Buenos Aires was always threatening to break away on the wings.

It was the second English loss to Buenos Aires, who also beat them in 1990, and adds a new foreign scalp to a distinguished collection including France in 1996 and South Africa in 1993. England beat Buenos Aires in 1981.
Every member of the Buenos Aires team which took the field on Saturday has played at least once for the Pumas.
England, who beat Argentine champions Cordoba on Wednesday 38-21, face Argentina "A" on Tuesday before they take on the Pumas in the first of two tests on Saturday.
The England squad has been sapped by the British Lions, who have taken 18 Englishmen on their tour of South Africa.
England - Tries: Clark, de Glanville, Mallinder. Penalties: King (2).
Buenos Aires - Tries: Solari. Penalties: Cilley (5). Dropped goal: Cilley.
